summary: Announcement of a Network Data Management meeting at MITRE on February 23 and 24, 1972. It aimed to hear about network data applications and to work toward a specification for a network data management protocol, using written proposals.

plainLanguage.summary: MITRE announced a Network Data Management meeting to discuss how network data facilities could help users. A working session would consider written proposals for a data-sharing protocol.

questions: what were the goals of the data management meeting
subtitle: A call for applications and protocol proposals at a data management meeting.

tldr.problem: The network community wanted to understand applications for data facilities and needed a concrete network data management protocol proposal.
tldr.mechanism: MITRE planned a meeting with application talks and a working session based on tentative written protocol proposals.
tldr.outcome: The meeting was intended to discuss applications and work toward a third-level data management protocol specification.

sections.title: Meeting Goals
sections.content:
MITRE planned to host a Network Data Management meeting on February 23-24. As a follow-up to the first data management meeting in August, it would focus on applications of network data facilities and on how networks could help users achieve their goals.

The second objective was to discuss and try to reach a specification for a network data management protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting had two goals: discuss uses for network data services and work toward a protocol specification. It followed earlier data management meetings.

sections.title: Application Talks
sections.content: The announced speakers planned to discuss medical file sharing, access to test results from medical testing centers, applications at Hughes Aircraft, distribution of NIC services through the network and MITRE's work on a system for the IRS. One speaker was still undecided.
sections.plainLanguage: Speakers would describe practical needs, including medical information, testing results and distributing NIC resources. These examples were intended to inform the protocol discussion.

sections.title: Protocol Working Session
sections.content:
The organizers planned to discuss tentative written proposals and hoped to make copies available before the meeting. Other interested people were encouraged to submit a third-level protocol for sharing network data.

Attendance was limited because facilities were limited and part of the meeting was a working session. Priority would go to people or representatives from groups that had taken part in earlier meetings.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants would review written proposals and work on a protocol design. Attendance was limited, with priority for groups that had joined previous meetings.
